events.text:
## Recommendation

- **Go to South Haven's pier.** My expected pier rating is **1 (below average)**. Ratings for all four: South Haven 1, Grand Haven 1, St. Joseph 1 (low confidence, no recent pier report), Muskegon 0.
- Cast spinners or spoons, and try shrimp under a bobber. Glow spoons were the most-cited lure on the Grand Haven and Muskegon piers.
- If South Haven is slow, Grand Haven is the next stop. Muskegon has had the slowest piers.
- Expect slow fishing. Plan on a few fish, not a steady bite.

## Why

- The two most recent pier reports at South Haven and Grand Haven both point to slow-to-fair pier fishing: Grand Haven was rated 1, and the South Haven coho pier report from Aug 27 was rated 2 (shrimp under bobbers, spinners and spoons).
- Muskegon's last two pier reports were both rated 0 (slow), so I'd expect it to be the weakest pier this week.
- I'd expect St. Joseph's pier to be slow, since no St. Joseph pier report appears in the last four weeks. Past St. Joseph September pier reports were mostly slow (2022, 2023, 2024), with one good week in 2024 (Sept 11).
- I'd expect the piers to stay slow because the pier-water temperature was flat and little upwelling wind showed up in the last 3 days, so there's no fresh cold-water push toward the piers (the week-before summary).

## Evidence

**Recent reports (newest is 2025-09-10, six days old)**
- South Haven, Aug 27: coho on the pier, quality 2. "Pier fishing was decent as well… spinners and spoons, as well as shrimp fished under bobbers." (South Haven, 2025-08-27)
- South Haven, Sept 10: a few kings and steelhead, "overall, fishing was slow… Most of the fish were caught by casting spoons." The method isn't stated. (South Haven, 2025-09-10)
- Grand Haven, Sept 10: pier quality 1. "Pier action was slow… A few were caught on gizzard shad or while casting glow spoons." (Grand Haven, 2025-09-10)
- Grand Haven, Sept 3: coho on pier, quality 1, "glow spoons or while using bobbers with gizzard shad." (Grand Haven, 2025-09-03)
- Muskegon, Sept 10: pier quality 0, "Pier anglers casting for salmon found the action slow." (Muskegon, 2025-09-10)
- Muskegon, Sept 3: pier quality 0, "Anglers casting from the piers found the salmon bite to be slow." (Muskegon, 2025-09-03)
- St. Joseph: no salmon pier report since Aug 27. Its latest boat report (Aug 27) was rated 2 and fish were "very spread out" on spoons near 70 ft. (St. Joseph, 2025-08-27)
- Boats, for reference: Muskegon (Sept 10) found salmon 70-150 ft down in 150-220 ft of water on green or white flies, not rated. (Muskegon, 2025-09-10)

**Past seasons (history, similar water around 69 F)**
- Piers at similar temperatures were mostly slow: Sept 2022, 2023 and 2024 pier reports at all four ports were mostly 0. (Grand Haven, 2022-09-14; St. Joseph, 2024-09-18; South Haven, 2023-09-27)
- The exception: St. Joseph pier, Sept 11, 2024, rated 3 (good) on spinners and spoons. "Pier anglers were catching good numbers of salmon." (St. Joseph, 2024-09-11)

**Conditions**
- The tool returned a backtest summary for the week before today, not live conditions. No current buoy reading, no cold-layer depth and no 3-day wind forecast came back.
- That week, the buoy showed about 68-69 F at all four ports, and the pier-water satellite reading was also about 68-69 F with no change over the last 3 days. (St. Joseph, South Haven, Grand Haven, Muskegon, week before 2025-09-16)
- Upwelling wind (north-to-east, 8+ mph) in the last 3 days: Grand Haven 6 h, Muskegon 12 h, St. Joseph 14 h, South Haven 15 h. (Same summary)

## Caveats

- The newest report is six days old, and the conditions data is from the week before today, not live. Check the current forecast and water before going.
- There's no recent St. Joseph pier report, so its rating of 1 is a guess based on history.
- The South Haven Sept 10 catch doesn't say where it was caught, so that report doesn't confirm pier fishing there.
- Ratings reflect expectations from older reports and history, not confirmed current fishing.
